jobs.completion: The selected track, artist, key and duration update together.

jobs.task: Play a track, seek to its middle and adjust monitoring level.
jobs.completion: Real audio time, selection, progress and gain controls agree.

entities.label: Track
entities.description: Original locally synthesized demo with tempo, key, texture and PCM.

entities.label: Index
entities.description: Stable library ordering used by previous and next.

entities.label: Oscilloscope
entities.description: Audio time-domain signal, with a buffered snapshot on pause.

states.description: Selected track is ready. Position and buffered signal are visible.
Audio advances and scope follows the current source.
The failed operation shows a status and playback can be retried.

transitions.effect: Resume audio context and start the current track.
Preserve playback position and show a still time-domain trace.
Reset position and keep playing with the updated selection in both library projections.
Cue the new track while preserving pause.
Expose recovery action in the controls.
Attempt playback again under a user gesture.

alternatives.name: Signal map and transport
alternatives.model: Tracks are points in tempo and texture space with an equivalent ordered index.
alternatives.navigation: Select a map point for discovery or use the named index, then seek within the selected recording.
alternatives.hardCase: Find a sparse track below 90 BPM, compare with the denser track near 120 BPM and jump midway.
alternatives.tradeoff: Exposes musical contrast immediately. Close points require an index or clustering as the library grows.

alternatives.name: Continuous reel
alternatives.model: One composite timeline with contiguous recordings and intervals.
alternatives.navigation: Drag or move the playhead to a passage, use interval markers to cue adjacent clips.
alternatives.hardCase: Compare adjacent parts and reorder a run of clips while holding a reference passage.
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast for listening in sequence. Random access by texture requires a second index.
